card.name: Kazukuta
card.tagline: Luanda's masked carnival dance with cane and umbrella
card.profile: Kazukuta is a traditional dance of Luanda, central to the city's Carnival, performed in groups (often in circles) to drums, marimbas and occasional brass. Its characteristic step is a slow tap-dance: the dancer shifts weight between heel and toe while leaning on a cane or umbrella (Mundo da Dança; Paraná State arts portal). Dancers wear striped trousers and ornamented military-style jackets and masks caricaturing animals to lampoon the oppressor, and the rhythm is kept on cans, dikanzas, bottles and barrel hoops.
card.insight: Together with semba, rebita and kabetula, kazukuta is one of the Luanda dance-music styles that fed into modern Angolan music; historically it served as a form of veiled protest, letting Angolans mock colonial authority through masquerade (FM Afro; Música de Angola).
